g.text: On the left the 14 people holding the most board seats, on the right the 32 firms that at least 3 of them sit on — the raw material of every interlock, before projection. Each edge is one observed directorship rather than

an inference: the one-mode graph the rest of this repository draws is made by joining two firms whenever a point on the left touches both. It is also why one badly resolved person moves a great many edges. Both

columns are ordered to minimise edge crossings, not by any grouping imposed here; that the Indochina firms end up together at the top and the Moroccan ones at the bottom is a result of the ordering rather than an
input to it. The identifiers with no initial — “paris” — are bare surnames resolution could not attach rather than people; they stay visible.
